newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan market steady in select demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan market steady in select demand.

text.p: Jordan's stock market was steady on Monday with some speculative buying of stocks being eyed by foreign funds in otherwise quiet trade, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.52 percent to 152.44 points.
Two large bloc sales were behind the high turnover of 1,984,614 dinars ($2.8 million), with Housing Bank's deal, valued at 931,623 dinars, alone accounting for nearly half the daily volume.
The top price gainers were National Steel and Jordan Phosphate Mines with a 5.08 percent rise to 1.24 dinars and a 3.15 percent price hike to 3.27 dinars respectively.

Dealers said market sentiment was also raised with comments by the stock market's head, Wahib al-Shair, on Sunday in which he expressed optimism that 1997 will witness higher global fund buying in the bourse.
Market heavyweight, Arab Bank, rose 4.00 dinars to 255 dinars, helping to underpin the official index.

Dealers said continued buying by major shareholders in Middle East Investment Bank kept up the activity on the stock which has lately improved on market speculation a French bank is considering an equity stake. It rose 0.02 dinars to 1.14 dinars on large 165,114 dinar turnover.
The market is currently underpinned by brighter performance of industrials that stand to benefit from exports to Iraq, which helped give the market a good New Year kick-off on Saturday.
Unified Transport Company, one of the companies that are expected to benefit from expanded transport cargo, rose 0.04 dinars to 2.15 dinars, with 92,787 dinars worth of shares exchanging hands.

Investors hopes were raised of business opportunities in the Iraqi market that could breathe new life into the Amman bourse after recent orders exceeding $100 million were secured by leading Jordanian firms under the oil-for-food deal.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.03 percent to 82.63 points from 82.61 points.
Losing shares outnumbered gainers on Monday by 17 to 12, with shares in eleven other firms trading but closing unchanged.
